nodes.content: Learn classifiers that reject shifting spurious cues without environment labels while preserving stable predictive features specific to minority groups.
requirements: Specify identifiability conditions distinguishing unstable shortcuts from stable minority-specific signals.
Improve worst-group accuracy ≥5 percentage points over ERM while losing ≤1 percentage point overall.

nodes.content: Propose OverlapGuard: infer environments from class-conditioned residuals, penalizing feature instability only within subgroups represented across environments.
Without environment labels, when do subgroup overlap and class-conditioned residual shifts identify shortcuts without suppressing stable minority predictors?
If class-conditioned residual anchors distinguish two regimes containing minority examples, shortcut-label associations shift while minority-predictor associations remain invariant.
On ShiftMix-v1, vary residual-anchor separation and minority-regime overlap; compare inferred shortcut shifts, minority-feature invariance, and worst-group/overall accuracy against ERM.
On ShiftMix-v1 (separable anchors, ≥15% minority overlap), OverlapGuard identified 89% shifting shortcuts, retained 94% minority predictors; worst-group +6.2pp, overall −0.4pp.
Advance OverlapGuard to real-data testing where anchors separate and minority overlap reaches 15%; ShiftMix-v1 met both accuracy targets.
Check Waterbirds/CelebA anchor separation and ≥15% minority overlap; conditionally benchmark OverlapGuard versus ERM for ≥5pp worst-group gain, ≤1pp overall loss.
Fit two-component residual mixtures on Waterbirds/CelebA without environment labels; measure anchor silhouette and minority overlap using held-out subgroup audits.
ResidualAudit-v1 reports Waterbirds/CelebA mixture assignments, anchor silhouettes, and held-out minority-overlap estimates for eligibility screening.
How can overlap-gated penalties avoid suppressing stable minority predictors when inferred residual clusters partially encode minority identity?
Audit ResidualAudit-v1 cluster assignments for minority identity leakage; sweep overlap gates to measure minority-feature retention and shortcut suppression.
On Waterbirds, ≥15% overlap gating retained 91% stable minority predictors and suppressed 83% shortcuts despite cluster–minority AUC 0.64.
Propose PairSwap: infer nuisance swaps from label-matched neighbors across latent clusters, enforcing invariance only when rare-cluster class margins persist.
Verify label-matched nuisance swaps, shifting shortcut correlations, and stable minority margins before PairSwap; test ≥5pp worst-group gain, ≤1pp overall loss.
Using ResidualAudit-v1 assignments, audit Waterbirds label-matched swaps for nuisance changes and stable minority margins; benchmark eligible PairSwap against ERM.
PairSwapAudit-v1 contains Waterbirds swap eligibility, nuisance-change rates, minority-margin stability, and eligible-model worst-group and overall accuracy versus ERM.
Reaudit PairSwapAudit-v1 nuisance swaps and bootstrap Waterbirds PairSwap–ERM worst-group/overall accuracy gaps by minority-margin stability.
Among eligible Waterbirds pairs, 29% of PairSwap swaps altered minority predictors; worst-group +2.1pp, overall −1.6pp versus ERM.
Despite cluster–minority AUC 0.64, margin-stability filtering before overlap gating should reduce PairSwap’s minority-predictor corruption from 29% below 10%.
On Waterbirds, filter PairSwap pairs by minority-margin stability before ≥15% overlap gating; measure predictor corruption and ERM-relative accuracies.
On Waterbirds, margin-filtered PairSwap reduced minority-predictor corruption from 29% to 8%; worst-group accuracy rose 5.3pp, overall fell 0.7pp versus ERM.
Revive PairSwap only with margin-stability filtering and ≥15% overlap gating: Waterbirds meets accuracy targets and reduces predictor corruption to 8%.
Benchmark OverlapGuard and revived margin-filtered PairSwap against ERM on Waterbirds/CelebA; audit anchor separation, ≥15% overlap, minority margins, worst-group/overall accuracy.
Propose DriftProbe: infer pseudo-regimes from time-ordered unlabeled batches, penalizing drifting feature effects while exempting stable minority-slice margins.
Under what overlap conditions does unlabeled temporal drift identify shortcut shifts without mistaking minority-prevalence changes for predictor instability?
With ≥15% minority presence per batch and class-conditional overlap, prevalence-reweighted effect drift identifies shortcuts while preserving stable minority margins.
Using PairSwapAudit-v1 margin annotations, simulate Waterbirds-Time batches varying minority prevalence and class overlap; evaluate DriftProbe shortcut recall and margin retention.
On Waterbirds-Time, despite ≥15% minority presence and class-conditional overlap, DriftProbe achieved 81% shortcut recall but 72% minority-margin retention after reweighting.
With class-by-minority support overlap and anchors conditionally independent of minority identity, DriftProbe should retain ≥90% minority margins while identifying shortcuts.
On Waterbirds-Time, vary audit-only class-by-minority support and conditional anchor leakage; measure DriftProbe minority-margin retention and shortcut recall.
On Waterbirds-Time, ≥10% per class-by-minority cell and conditional anchor–minority AUC ≤0.52 yielded 92% minority-margin retention; shortcut recall 83%.
Prioritize margin-filtered PairSwap; restrict DriftProbe to ≥10% class-by-minority cells and anchor AUC ≤0.52 pending accuracy testing.
Waterbirds-Time-v1 package contains prevalence-controlled batches, class-by-minority support audits, conditional anchor-leakage scores, and DriftProbe retention/shortcut-recall results.
Propose CueSurgery: use diffusion-edited background counterfactuals, enforcing invariance only when rare-cluster class margins survive edits.
Using Waterbirds-Time-v1, benchmark CueSurgery and eligible DriftProbe against ERM; audit edit fidelity, minority-margin retention, worst-group and overall accuracy.
On Waterbirds-Time-v1, CueSurgery retained 93% minority margins; versus ERM, worst-group accuracy rose 5.8pp and overall fell 0.6pp.
Advance CueSurgery (+5.8pp worst-group, −0.6pp overall); gate DriftProbe by ≥10% cell support and anchor AUC ≤0.52.
Benchmark CueSurgery and gated DriftProbe on held-out CelebA/Waterbirds shifts; require stable minority margins, ≥5pp worst-group gain, ≤1pp overall loss.
Train CueSurgery and eligibility-gated DriftProbe on CelebA/Waterbirds; audit minority-margin retention and bootstrap ERM-relative worst-group/overall accuracy under held-out shifts.
HeldoutShiftReport-v1 contains CelebA/Waterbirds eligibility audits, minority-margin retention, and bootstrapped worst-group/overall accuracy gaps versus ERM.
Independently audit HeldoutShiftReport-v1: verify eligibility thresholds, minority-margin stability, and 95% bootstrap intervals against both accuracy targets.
Audited HeldoutShiftReport-v1 eligible shifts: CueSurgery worst-group +5.6pp (95% CI +5.1–6.2), overall −0.6pp (−0.9–−0.3) versus ERM; minority-margin retention 92%.
Can CueSurgery’s margin gate detect diffusion edits that change stable minority features despite preserving the predicted class?
CueSurgery’s rare-cluster margin gate flags ≥90% of class-preserving edits that alter minority features, with ≤10% false positives.
Class-preserving edits to minority-specific textures leave rare-cluster margins nearly unchanged, causing ≥20% of feature changes to escape CueSurgery’s gate.
Propose TetherDRO: reweight high-loss latent clusters while preserving rare-subtype predictions through distillation restricted to augmentation-consistent examples.
Annotate 500 class-preserving CueSurgery edits for minority-feature changes; validate margin-gate sensitivity and augmentation consistency before TetherDRO distillation.
Using HeldoutShiftReport-v1, annotate 500 class-preserving edits; measure gate sensitivity, false positives, missed changes, and consistency-gated TetherDRO accuracy versus ERM.
In 500 annotated edits, CueSurgery’s margin gate missed 24% of minority-feature changes; sensitivity 76%, false-positive rate 8%.
Prioritize margin-filtered PairSwap; retain CueSurgery only with minority-feature edit audits, since accuracy gains coexist with 24% undetected changes.
Replace margin-gate validation with cross-fitted minority-feature-change detection on 500 annotated edits; gate CueSurgery/TetherDRO and benchmark against prioritized PairSwap.
Five-fold cross-fit a minority-feature-change detector on 500 edits; gate CueSurgery/TetherDRO and benchmark worst-group/overall accuracy against PairSwap and ERM.
EditGuard-v1 includes cross-fitted minority-feature-change predictions, fold-separated gate thresholds, and CueSurgery/TetherDRO versus PairSwap/ERM accuracy tables.
Audit EditGuard-v1 fold separation and minority-change recall; bootstrap held-out CelebA worst-group and overall accuracy gaps against PairSwap and ERM.
EditGuard-v1 recalled 93% minority-feature changes; on held-out CelebA, gated CueSurgery/TetherDRO gained 5.9/5.2pp worst-group, lost 0.5/0.8pp overall versus ERM.
